intro: NLP text ko numbers aur structure me badalne ka naam hai. Is section me tokenization, frequency, stopwords, n-grams, vocabulary, cosine similarity aur softmax jaise building blocks pure Python me likhe jate hain — transformers inhi ideas par bade scale par kaam karte hain.
theory: Tokenization text ko chhote units me todta hai (words/subwords). Model jo tokens dekhta hai wahi uska universe hai; unknown words ka handling vocabulary size aur OOV se juda hai.
Text normalization (lowercase, punctuation) matching ko predictable banata hai, par kabhi case ya punctuation meaning rakhta hai — task ke hisaab se faisla karo.
Bag-of-words frequency order bhool jata hai; n-grams thoda context jodte hain. TF-IDF common words ka weight kam karta hai aur distinctive words ko high.
Embedding text ko vector banata hai; cosine similarity do vectors ka angle measure karti hai, magnitude ignore karti hai.
Softmax scores ko probability distribution me badalta hai; temperature se distribution sharp ya flat hoti hai.
syntax:
from transformers import pipeline

classifier = pipeline("sentiment-analysis")
print(classifier("Pandas makes cleaning fun"))

from transformers import AutoTokenizer

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("bert-base-uncased")
encoded = tokenizer("hello world", return_tensors="pt")
print(encoded["input_ids"].shape)

from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer

vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer()
matrix = vectorizer.fit_transform(documents)
print(matrix.shape)

examples.code:
import math
from collections import Counter

chunks = {
    'c1': 'pandas groupby aggregation summary',
    'c2': 'numpy array broadcasting axis',
    'c3': 'pandas merge join keys',
}
query = 'pandas groupby'
q_tokens = Counter(query.split())

scores = {}
for name, text in chunks.items():
    t_tokens = Counter(text.split())
    dot = sum(q_tokens[t] * t_tokens[t] for t in q_tokens)
    q_norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in q_tokens.values()))
    t_norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in t_tokens.values()))
    scores[name] = round(dot / (q_norm * t_norm), 3) if dot else 0.0

print(sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda item: item[1], reverse=True))
explain: Keyword-vector cosine scoring se query ke sabse relevant chunk ka ranking banti hai.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Support tickets ka routing keywords + embeddings dono se hota hai: keyword fast hai, embedding semantic similarity pakadta hai.
Search/RAG me chunking aur top-k retrieval quality poore system ka ceiling decide karti hai.
Sentiment/moderation models ke input ko normalize karna padta hai, warna casing aur punctuation predictions badal dete hain.

interview.q: Tokenization me word-level aur subword-level ka fark kya hai?
interview.a: Word-level vocabulary bada aur OOV-prone hota hai; subword (BPE/WordPiece) rare words ko pieces me todta hai, isliye vocabulary chhota rehta hai aur unseen words bhi represent ho jate hain.

interview.q: TF-IDF kis problem ko solve karta hai?
interview.a: Raw counts common words ko dominate karne dete hain. IDF un terms ka weight kam karta hai jo bahut documents me aate hain, isliye distinctive terms highlight hote hain.

interview.q: Cosine similarity Euclidean distance se kab better hai?
interview.a: Jab vector ki length (document length) matter na kare, sirf direction/content matter kare. Embeddings me cosine standard hai; magnitude meaningful ho to Euclidean bhi theek hai.

interview.q: Temperature sampling me kya hota hai?
interview.a: Logits ko temperature se divide karke softmax lagate hain: low temperature sharp/deterministic, high temperature flat/random. Ye creativity aur reliability ka knob hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye NLP + Transformers ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'
debugging.why: int() sirf poore number ka string parse karta hai. Ye NLP + Transformers ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

debugging.why: String immutable hai; append list ka method hai. Ye NLP + Transformers ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: String concatenation ya join use karo.
debugging.lesson: AttributeError galat type par method call ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Naam ki spelling galat hai; Python namespace me wo naam nahi milta. Ye NLP + Transformers ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: NameError typo ya missing assignment batata hai.
